newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German M3 grows 8.4 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German M3 grows 8.4 pct in October.

text.p: Following are reactions to a report from the Bundesbank that October M3 money supply grew an annualised 8.4 percent compared with 8.4 percent in September. The figure was in line with market expectations.

ARMIN KAYSER, SWISS BANK CORP, FRANKFURT: "It looks like they will have a neutral impact on the market. The Bundesbank had warned that the initial public offering of Deutsche Telekom would have an extensive effect on the data. It is difficult to tell if this was the case. We have seen a pretty strong acceleration in M3 over the last few months.

"Although the Bundesbank will see this as an aberration, the underlying trends in credit growth have accelerated, but they are still in a region where there is no real course for concern. It will have no impact on policy."

HOLGER SCHMIEDING, MERRILL LYNCH, FRANKFURT: "It was slightly more than what the market had been expecting. But once the market looks at the details, it should have a neutral impact. Several Bundesbankers had warned of the Telekom impact so that was not a surprise. The figure is not a problem for the Bundesbank. M3 should start to moderate again from December."

ULRICH BECKMANN, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT DB RESEARCH: "The figure is good, but you should not get too excited about it. It was at the upper end of our forecast. The number was boosted by the Telekom issue. Without that effect it would have been a little lower." He added that 8.2 percent growth for November "would be reasonable guess. There is no need for a rate cut any more. The economy is improving."
